Supplementary Forms A–E
Origin of the instruments (Forms A–D). The interview guide and the three questionnaires were developed entirely by the author for this study from the research questions and the literature reviewed in the article. They are not adapted or reproduced from any third-party instrument and contain no third-party material requiring a licence or permission. 
Supplementary Form A: Interview Guide (Semi-Structured)
Opening
Please describe your role in accreditation processes at your institution.
How long have you been involved in accreditation activities?
Accreditation Preparation
What activities does your institution undertake in preparation for accreditation?
Who is involved in these activities?
How would you describe the purpose of accreditation preparation?
Accreditation Effects
What changes, if any, have you observed as a result of accreditation?
How has accreditation affected teaching and learning?
How has accreditation affected institutional resources and infrastructure?
How has accreditation affected internal quality assurance processes?
Motivation and Engagement
Why does your institution engage with accreditation?
What would happen if accreditation were not mandatory?
How would you describe the attitudes of colleagues toward accreditation?
Internal Quality Assurance
How would you describe the role of the Quality Assurance Unit at your institution?
How are quality assurance activities integrated into daily academic life?
What challenges exist in implementing internal quality assurance?
Divergent Perspectives
Are there any positive aspects of accreditation that are often overlooked?
Are there any negative aspects that are often overlooked?
Closing
Is there anything else you would like to add?
Supplementary Form B: Questionnaire Instrument (University Leaders)
Section A: Background Information
Institution type: Public / Private
Role: Vice-Chancellor / Registrar / QA Officer / Accreditation Desk Officer / Senior Lecturer
Years in current role:
Years involved in accreditation:
Section B: Accreditation Preparation
Describe the activities your institution undertakes in preparation for accreditation.
Who is involved in accreditation preparation?
Approximately how much time do you personally spend on accreditation-related tasks per week?
Section C: Accreditation Effects
What changes have you observed as a result of accreditation? (Please describe)
How has accreditation affected teaching and learning at your institution?
How has accreditation affected institutional resources and infrastructure?
How has accreditation affected internal quality assurance processes?
Section D: Motivation and Engagement
Why does your institution engage with accreditation?
What would happen if accreditation were not mandatory?
How would you describe the attitudes of colleagues toward accreditation?
Section E: Internal Quality Assurance
How would you describe the role of the Quality Assurance Unit at your institution?
How are quality assurance activities integrated into daily academic life?
What challenges exist in implementing internal quality assurance?
Section F: Open Comments
Please provide any additional comments on accreditation and quality culture at your institution.
Supplementary Form C: Questionnaire Instrument (Students)
Section A: Background Information
Institution type: Public / Private
Level of study: Undergraduate / Postgraduate
Programme of study:
Year of study:
Section B: Awareness of Accreditation
Are you aware of accreditation processes at your institution? Yes / No
If yes, how did you learn about them?
Section C: Perceived Effects of Accreditation
Have you observed any changes at your institution related to accreditation? (Please describe)
How has accreditation affected your learning experience?
How has accreditation affected teaching practices?
How has accreditation affected library and laboratory resources?
How has accreditation affected student support services?
Section D: Open Comments
Please provide any additional comments on accreditation and quality at your institution.
Note: The student questionnaire contained no items on internal QA or administrative workload, and no dedicated items on curriculum formalisation or compliance motivation. Student evidence on the last two themes could arise only in unprompted open comments (Sections C and D); it could not be verified against retained responses and is not reported in Table 2 (NE).
Supplementary Form D: Questionnaire Instrument (Assessors)
Section A: Background Information
Years of experience as a GTEC assessor:
Number of institutions assessed:
Types of institutions assessed: Public / Private / Both
Section B: Observations from Assessments
What patterns have you observed across institutions regarding accreditation preparation?
What changes do institutions typically make in response to accreditation?
How would you describe the relationship between documentation and practice in the institutions you assess?
What challenges do institutions face in sustaining quality improvement between accreditation cycles?
Section C: Quality Culture
Based on your experience, how would you describe the quality culture in Ghanaian universities?
What factors promote or hinder the development of quality culture?
What changes would you recommend to the accreditation system?
Section D: Open Comments
Please provide any additional comments on accreditation and quality culture in Ghanaian higher education.
Supplementary Form E: Summary of ethical approval details
Ethics Committee | UNISA (University of South Africa) College of Education Ethics Review Committee
Reference Number | 2023/07/05/10084665/05/AM
Approval Date | 5 July 2023
Approval Type | Full ethical clearance
Conditions of Approval | Informed consent must be obtained from all participants; confidentiality and anonymity must be maintained; participants have the right to withdraw at any time; data must be stored securely according to institutional protocols.
Compliance | All conditions of approval were met during the conduct of this study.
This form summarises the approval details only which is supplied confidentially to the editor (not for review; not for publication). Signed consent records and institutional permission letters are likewise held confidentially.
